theme: wildcard: a national tourism-statistics official who knows which agenc
ideas: 1. National tourism-board / national statistical office SDMX endpoints (many smaller countries publish monthly arrivals, nights, receipts via SDMX rather than a bespoke API) and the generic SDMX client libraries that make ANY of these machine-pullable.

2. Central-bank / national-payment-system card-spend or foreign-currency-cash-withdrawal statistics used domestically as a tourist-spend proxy (Bank of Thailand, Banco de Mexico, BBVA/CaixaBank, Norges Bank, ONS/BoE card data).
3. Utility (electricity/water) open data as an occupancy proxy for vacation homes / STR units in tourist-heavy zip codes or second-home-heavy counties.
4. Telecom-regulator roaming / inbound-SIM statistics used by national tourism boards to estimate visitor volumes and dwell time.

5. Cruise-line advance-ticket-sale disclosures and port-call / passenger-arrival records as a 'book-ahead' business analogue and as a regional demand proxy for cruise-adjacent STR markets (Caribbean, Mediterranean).
6. National housing-census 'vacant for seasonal/recreational use' or second-home stock registries as an STR-supply proxy independent of Inside Airbnb scraping.
7. National weather-service tropical-cyclone/hurricane track archives (HURDAT2-type) as event-shock data for cancellations/RNPL and regional booking disruption in hurricane-season markets.
8. National tourism satellite account (TSA/UNWTO-style) compilation tooling, which aggregates nights/output ratios across many countries in one pull.
9. Port-authority / transportation-authority open datasets (container and passenger throughput) as a proxy for regional travel and trade activity feeding into regional-mix forecasts.
10. Municipal/state tourist or bed-tax and transient-occupancy-tax filing datasets beyond the ones already catalogued, especially non-US jurisdictions.

candidates.name: rsdmx
candidates.what_it_holds: R package/client for reading SDMX-ML and SDMX-JSON data and metadata from any SDMX-compliant provider (Eurostat, OECD, IMF, ILO, UNSD, and many national statistical/tourism offices that publish via SDMX). Not a dataset itself; a generic connector. 110 stars, actively used, GPL-ish/open license, maintained multi-year.
candidates.why_useful: Lets us systematically pull monthly tourism arrivals/nights/receipts and accommodation-capacity series from dozens of national statistics agencies (gap #7 LatAm/APAC volume, gap #4 point-in-time vintages if the provider keeps dataflow versions) instead of one country at a time.
candidates.time_coverage: varies by provider, typically monthly, multi-year
candidates.size_hint: connector library, not a fixed dataset

candidates.name: sdmx1 (python-sdmx)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python implementation of the SDMX information model plus a client (`sdmx1` on PyPI) for querying SDMX REST APIs across many national and international statistical agencies. 47 stars, part of the official SDMX-IM ecosystem, actively maintained.
candidates.why_useful: Same rationale as rsdmx but Python-native, fits our pandas/DuckDB pipeline directly; could be the harness for pulling non-US/EU national tourism arrivals series at scale (gap #7).

candidates.name: opensdmx
candidates.what_it_holds: Python CLI and library supporting multiple SDMX REST API dialects, aimed at discovering and pulling dataflows across providers that don't share one exact SDMX flavor. 52 stars.
candidates.why_useful: Discovery layer for finding which national tourism/statistics agencies expose SDMX data at all — useful as a first pass before hand-wiring per-country pulls (complements gap #17's Socrata/CKAN-discovery idea, applied to SDMX).
candidates.last_activity: unknown, seen active in topic listing

candidates.name: pysdmx
candidates.what_it_holds: Bank for International Settlements-maintained Python SDMX library (29 stars) for reading/writing SDMX data and metadata, used internally at BIS and by some central banks for statistical exchange.
candidates.why_useful: A central-bank-grade SDMX client is a plausible route into central-bank tourism-receipts or card-spend series (gap #6) that are published via SDMX rather than a bespoke portal.

candidates.name: restatapi
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Eurostat R package (35 stars) to search and retrieve ANY Eurostat SDMX dataset, not just tour_ce_omr platform nights — includes accommodation capacity, occupancy rate by NUTS2 region, nights spent by country of residence, and tourism-industry employment tables.
candidates.why_useful: Finer-grained/regional (NUTS2) version of the Eurostat platform-nights series we already hold; could give sub-national EMEA occupancy and nights-by-origin-country splits that tour_ce_omr alone doesn't, useful for regional-mix forecasting.
candidates.size_hint: connector library over Eurostat's full catalogue
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Extends what we hold (Eurostat tour_ce_omr monthly platform nights) — finer regional grain and additional dataflows, not a duplicate.

candidates.name: hurdat-hadisst-data
candidates.what_it_holds: R package bundling a unified, cleaned dataset merging NOAA HURDAT2 tropical-cyclone tracks/intensity with HadISST1 sea-surface-temperature data for the North Atlantic and Northeast Pacific basins. Data + R/ code + data-raw/ + processed data/ folders, GPL-3.0, 2 stars (small, academic thesis project) but the underlying HURDAT2 source is NOAA-official and goes back to 1851 (Atlantic) / 1949 (E. Pacific).
candidates.why_useful: Hurricane-season event/shock data for Florida, Gulf Coast, and Caribbean STR markets — feeds cancellation/RNPL and regional-mix disruption modeling around the Q3/Q4 guide window (gap #11 events and shocks).
candidates.geography: North Atlantic and NE Pacific basins
candidates.time_coverage: HURDAT2 source back to 1851/1949; package itself thesis-scoped, may be a subset
candidates.size_hint: small R package with bundled CSV/RData
candidates.last_activity: low activity, 11 commits total, exact date not surfaced

candidates.name: Ahead-of-the-Storm-DATAPIPELINE
candidates.what_it_holds: UNICEF Data & Predictive Analytics pipeline that ingests and processes tropical-storm/hurricane 'envelope' geospatial data for impact analysis (originally built for child-population exposure, but the storm-track/impact-footprint ingestion is domain-agnostic). 2 stars.
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made pipeline pattern for turning storm tracks into geographic exposure footprints, which could be repointed at STR-market exposure (which Inside Airbnb markets/zip codes sit inside a given storm's cone) for the RNPL/cancellation thesis (gap #11, #3).
candidates.time_coverage: depends on storm data source ingested (likely NOAA/IBTrACS-based)
candidates.size_hint: pipeline code, not a fixed dataset

candidates.name: thailand-statistics-analyzer
candidates.what_it_holds: Python tool (src/ modules for list/get/search/analyze) that pulls official Thai government statistics via SDMX, including international tourist arrivals plus population/economy/labor/transport series, bilingual (English/Thai) JSON output, sample data and outputs committed under data/.
candidates.why_useful: Concrete route into Thailand's national tourism-arrivals data (APAC volume, gap #7) without hand-rolling an SDMX query against NSO Thailand; very low maturity (0 stars, 1 commit) so treat as a starting point/proof of API existence rather than a finished pipeline.
candidates.time_coverage: whatever Thai NSO SDMX dataflow covers (likely monthly, multi-year)
candidates.last_activity: very recent (2025), but only 1 commit — unverified maintenance

candidates.name: d3-stacked-bar-massport-carriers
candidates.what_it_holds: D3.js visualization repo with underlying data on container-carrier alliances serving the Massachusetts Port Authority (MassPort) FY2014-FY2020 — cargo/container throughput by carrier, not passenger or cruise traffic.
candidates.why_useful: Weak fit: only port-authority repo surfaced under that topic, and it's cargo-container data, not passenger/cruise arrivals, so it doesn't speak to tourism volume directly. Flagging as a dead end for the 'port authority' angle rather than a real lead.
